key_insight: Standard RL optimizes expected returns under a training distribution and can miss low-probability but safe states; this paper develops an RL-based framework that discovers whether a parametric 'avoid' safety requirement is feasible and, when feasible, learns policies that are robust across parameter variations.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between reachability-style safety objectives (maximize the set of initial states that avoid unsafe regions for all time) and policy-learning under unknown parameter uncertainty and unknown feasibility — i.e., determining if a robust safe policy exists and, if so, synthesizing one that performs across the full parameter set rather than just on average.
method: Formulate the parameter-robust avoid problem with an explicit notion of unknown feasibility and convert it into an RL-compatible objective that emphasizes worst-case / low-probability parameter performance rather than expected reward.
Use an adversarial or parameter-sampling curriculum to search parameter space and a safety critic / feasibility detector to identify infeasible regimes or certify candidate policies.

Train policies with robustness-promoting learning (e.g., minimax or risk-sensitive updates and heavy penalty for entering unsafe states), iterating between feasibility assessment and policy improvement.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical path to synthesize controllers that are robust to parameter uncertainty and to detect when safety specs are unattainable — improving reliability for safety-critical systems where rare parameter settings matter as much as average-case performance.
visual_elements: Two-panel schematic: (left) training distribution vs. full parameter space highlighting low-probability safe regions missed by standard RL; (right) target robust safe set covering all parameters.
Flowchart of the method: parameter sampling/adversary → feasibility detector → robust-RL loop → policy certification/failure report.
Heatmap over parameter space showing safety outcome (safe/unsafe/infeasible) before and after applying the proposed method.
Plot comparing expected-return optimization vs. worst-case / robust objective performance across parameter perturbations (show improved worst-case safety)
paper_title: Solving Parameter-Robust Avoid Problems with Unknown Feasibility using Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Oswin So, Eric Yang Yu, Songyuan Zhang, Matthew Cleaveland, Mitchell Black
